scores.rationale: Returning the image unchanged is straightforward and easy to understand for any stakeholder.
Creating a uniform white image is simple but its clinical utility requires some inference.
Creating a blank/black image is simple but its clinical purpose requires some inference.
Inverting image intensities (making bright areas dark and vice versa) is a familiar radiological concept.
Normalizing image values to a standard range is a recognizable preprocessing step in medical imaging.
Standardization using mean and standard deviation is statistically familiar but less intuitively visual.
Converting binary/segment images to intensity representation requires understanding of image type distinctions.
Shrinking bright regions is conceptually relatable to reducing highlighted structures in an image.
Expanding bright regions is conceptually relatable to enlarging highlighted structures in an image.
Removing small bright noise by erosion then dilation is clinically relevant but requires morphological knowledge.
Filling small dark gaps is clinically relevant (e.g., closing holes in lesions) but requires morphological knowledge.
Extracting small bright structures is relevant to detecting small lesions, though the transform name is technical.
Extracting small dark structures is clinically relevant but the black top-hat concept is less familiar.
Emphasizing object boundaries is directly relevant to lesion or tissue boundary delineation.
Morphological Laplace edge response is a highly technical concept unlikely to be familiar to a clinician.
Subtracting one image from another is intuitively understandable as highlighting differences between images.
Adding two images elementwise is intuitively understandable as combining image information.
Multiplying two images elementwise is somewhat intuitive as masking or weighting, though less immediate.
Taking the elementwise maximum between two images is moderately interpretable as selecting the brighter value.
Taking the elementwise minimum between two images is moderately interpretable as selecting the darker value.
Subtracting a constant from every pixel is easily understood as shifting brightness downward.
Adding a constant to every pixel is easily understood as shifting brightness upward.
Multiplying every pixel by a scalar is easily understood as adjusting image contrast or gain.
Sobel X derivative highlights vertical edges; the concept of edge detection is familiar but the specific filter name is technical.
Sobel Y derivative highlights horizontal edges; edge detection is familiar but the specific filter name is technical.
Sobel gradient magnitude highlights all edges/boundaries, which is clinically meaningful for structure delineation.
Ando filter is an obscure technical variant of derivative filters unlikely to be recognized by clinicians.
Ando filter is an obscure technical variant of derivative filters unlikely to be recognized by clinicians.
Ando gradient magnitude is a technical concept not recognizable to medical professionals.
Ando 4x4 filter variant is highly technical and not interpretable without CV expertise.
Ando 4x4 filter variant is highly technical and not interpretable without CV expertise.
Ando 4x4 gradient magnitude is a technical concept not recognizable to medical professionals.
Ando 5x5 filter variant is highly technical and not interpretable without CV expertise.
Ando 5x5 filter variant is highly technical and not interpretable without CV expertise.
Ando 5x5 gradient magnitude is a technical concept not recognizable to medical professionals.
Bickley filter is an obscure technical filter name with no clinical relevance or recognition.
Bickley filter is an obscure technical filter name with no clinical relevance or recognition.
Bickley gradient magnitude is an obscure technical concept with no clinical relevance.
Prewitt X derivative is a known edge detection filter but the name is technical and directional details require background.
Prewitt Y derivative is a known edge detection filter but the name is technical and directional details require background.
Prewitt gradient magnitude for edge detection is somewhat interpretable as boundary highlighting.
Scharr filter is a technical CV concept unlikely to be familiar to clinicians.
Scharr filter is a technical CV concept unlikely to be familiar to clinicians.
Scharr gradient magnitude highlights edges but the filter name remains technical for a clinician.
Gaussian smoothing/blurring at a specific scale is a familiar image processing concept in medical imaging.
Gaussian smoothing at a larger scale is interpretable as broader blurring of image details.
Gaussian smoothing at progressively larger kernel is interpretable as strong blurring.
Gaussian smoothing with a large kernel is interpretable as heavy blurring, though sigma values are technical.
Gaussian smoothing with a very large kernel is interpretable as very heavy blurring.
Laplacian edge detection is a known concept but the second-order derivative framing requires technical background.
Difference of Gaussians for edge/blob detection is a moderately known concept but technically named.
Moffat filter is an obscure technical filter from astrophysics with no recognizable clinical meaning.
Moffat filter is an obscure technical filter with no recognizable clinical meaning.
Moffat filter is an obscure technical filter with no recognizable clinical meaning.
Applying an exponential transform to pixel values is a recognized intensity transformation but its visual effect needs interpretation.
Log transform with sign inversion is a recognized enhancement technique but the inverted sign adds confusion.
Logarithmic intensity transformation to enhance dark regions is a familiar concept in medical image display.
Power-law (gamma) transformation of pixel values is a recognized image enhancement concept.
Conditional selection between two images based on a condition map is moderately interpretable as a masking operation.
Block-wise average pooling creating uniform regions is interpretable as a spatial averaging/downsampling concept.
Averaging only center row and column of blocks is a technical operation without clear clinical intuition.
Block-wise maximum pooling highlighting the brightest value in each region is moderately interpretable.
Max pooling over center row and column of blocks is a technical operation without clear clinical intuition.
Block-wise minimum pooling highlighting the darkest value in each region is moderately interpretable.
Min pooling over center row and column of blocks is a technical operation without clear clinical intuition.
Sliding-window mean pooling as local averaging is an interpretable spatial smoothing operation.
Sliding-window max pooling highlighting local bright spots is interpretable as detecting local bright features.
Sliding-window min pooling highlighting local dark spots is interpretable as detecting local dark features.
Sliding-window standard deviation maps local intensity variability, which is clinically relevant for texture.
Sliding-window median pooling as a noise-robust local average is an interpretable smoothing operation.
Counting unique values in local windows is a technical operation without direct clinical intuition.
Argmax-count pooling is a technical operation without clear clinical meaning.
Argmin-count pooling is a technical operation without clear clinical meaning.
Interquartile range pooling measures local intensity spread and is moderately interpretable as local contrast variability.
Gradient magnitude as a map of intensity changes is directly interpretable as edge/boundary strength in tissue.
Gradient orientation map showing the direction of intensity changes requires some geometric interpretation.
Selecting gradients near a specific orientation is a technical concept requiring knowledge of directional filtering.
Returning the image unchanged is straightforward and easy to understand for any stakeholder.
Creating a fully white binary image is simple but its clinical purpose requires some inference.
Creating a fully black binary image is simple but its clinical purpose requires some inference.
Inverting a binary image (swapping foreground and background) is intuitive and clinically understandable.
Converting to binary by thresholding is directly understandable as separating foreground from background.
Thresholding with a specified value to create a binary image is intuitive and clinically meaningful.
Subtracting two binary images is interpretable as finding regions present in one but not the other.
Adding two binary images is interpretable as combining or unioning two segmented regions.
Multiplying two binary images is interpretable as the intersection of two segmented regions.
Elementwise maximum of binary images is interpretable as logical OR (union of regions).
Elementwise minimum of binary images is interpretable as logical AND (intersection of regions).
Adaptive local thresholding to segment heterogeneous regions is a clinically meaningful concept.
Niblack thresholding is a named local method that requires background knowledge to distinguish from other methods.
Polysegment thresholding is a technical method name without obvious clinical intuition.
Sauvola thresholding is a named local method that requires background knowledge to distinguish from others.
Otsu thresholding is a widely known automatic histogram-based segmentation method recognizable in biomedical contexts.
Minimum-intermodes thresholding is a technical histogram method not immediately clear to a clinician.
Intermodes thresholding is a technical histogram method not immediately clear to a clinician.
Minimum-error thresholding is a statistical method that is not intuitively clear to a clinician.
Moments-based thresholding is a technical statistical method not immediately interpretable clinically.
Unimodal Rosin thresholding is a named technical method not familiar to most clinicians.
Entropy-based thresholding is a somewhat recognizable concept linking information content to segmentation.
Balanced histogram thresholding is partially intuitive but remains a technical method name.
Yen thresholding is a named technical method not familiar to most clinicians.
Manual thresholding with explicit parameters is highly interpretable as direct user-controlled segmentation.

Sobel Y edge detection binarized is moderately interpretable as detecting horizontal boundaries.
Sobel gradient magnitude binarized highlights all tissue/structure edges in a recognizable way.

Scharr filter is a technical CV concept unlikely to be familiar to clinicians.

Gaussian smoothing binarized is interpretable as detecting broad intensity features after blurring.
Gaussian smoothing at larger scale binarized is interpretable as detecting coarser intensity features.
Gaussian smoothing at progressively larger kernel binarized is interpretable as detecting very coarse features.
Large Gaussian smoothing binarized is interpretable as detecting broad regional intensity patterns.
Very large Gaussian smoothing binarized is interpretable as detecting very broad spatial patterns.
Laplacian edge detection binarized is moderately interpretable as marking sharp boundaries.
Difference of Gaussians binarized is a moderately known concept for detecting edges and blobs.

Moffat filter is an obscure technical filter with no recognizable clinical meaning.
Moffat filter is an obscure technical filter with no recognizable clinical meaning.
Marking local intensity minima is directly interpretable as identifying local dark spots or valleys in tissue.
Marking local intensity maxima is directly interpretable as identifying local bright spots or peaks in tissue.
Shrinking binary foreground regions is interpretable as reducing or trimming segmented structures.
Expanding binary foreground regions is interpretable as growing or enlarging segmented structures.
Removing small binary noise regions is clinically relevant for cleaning up segmentation results.
Filling small holes in binary regions is clinically relevant for completing segmented structures.
Extracting small bright binary structures is relevant to detecting small lesions, though the transform name is technical.
Extracting small dark binary structures is clinically relevant but the black top-hat concept is less familiar.
Emphasizing binary object boundaries is directly relevant to lesion edge delineation.
Morphological Laplace edge response is a highly technical concept unlikely to be familiar to a clinician.
Conditional selection between two binary images based on a condition map is moderately interpretable as conditional masking.
Block-wise average pooling of binary image measures local foreground density in a block.
Averaging center row and column of blocks is a technical operation without clear clinical intuition.
Block-wise max pooling of binary image marks any foreground presence in a block.
Max pooling over center row and column of blocks is a technical operation without clear clinical intuition.
Block-wise min pooling of binary image marks only fully foreground blocks.
Min pooling over center row and column of blocks is a technical operation without clear clinical intuition.
Sliding-window mean pooling on binary image measures local foreground density.
Sliding-window max pooling on binary image detects any foreground presence in a neighborhood.
Sliding-window min pooling on binary image marks fully foreground neighborhoods.
Standard deviation pooling on binary images measures local foreground variability, which is less directly intuitive.
Sliding-window median pooling on binary image is moderately interpretable as a robust local foreground measure.
Unique count pooling on binary images has limited intuitive clinical meaning.
Argmax-count pooling is a technical operation without clear clinical meaning.
Argmin-count pooling is a technical operation without clear clinical meaning.
IQR pooling on binary images measures local variability but has limited direct clinical interpretation.
Returning the segmentation image unchanged is straightforward and easy to understand.
Creating a uniform segment label image is simple but its role in a pipeline requires inference.
Creating a blank segment label image is simple but its role in a pipeline requires inference.
Converting binary to labeled segments separating background and foreground is interpretable in the context of tissue segmentation.
Region-labeling segmentation is interpretable as identifying distinct tissue regions, though the method name is technical.
Watershed segmentation is a well-known method in biomedical imaging for separating touching structures like cells.
Returning a value unchanged is universally understandable.
Returning a constant value of 1.0 is simple and universally understandable.
Hyperbolic tangent is a mathematical function familiar to those with quantitative training but not typical clinicians.
ReLU is a machine learning activation function not typically familiar to clinicians.
Modulo remainder is a basic arithmetic operation understandable to most but with unclear direct clinical meaning.
Checking equality between two values is a simple logical operation easily understood by any stakeholder.
Checking if one value is greater than another is a simple comparison understandable by any stakeholder.
Checking if one value is lower than another is a simple comparison understandable by any stakeholder.
Logical NOT returning 1 when input is at most 0.5 is somewhat interpretable as a binary inversion.
Adding two numbers is universally understandable.
Subtracting one number from another is universally understandable.
Multiplying two numbers is universally understandable.
Dividing two numbers is universally understandable, though the division-by-zero exception is a technical detail.
Safe division returning 0 on zero divisor is interpretable as a guarded ratio calculation.
Raising a number to a power is a familiar mathematical operation.
The mathematical constant pi is universally known.
Exponential function is familiar from scientific and medical contexts.
Natural logarithm is a familiar scientific function, though clipping details are technical.
Base-10 logarithm is familiar from scientific and medical contexts (e.g., pH, dB scales).
Returning the total number of pixels in an image is easily understood as image size.
Returning the largest image dimension is interpretable as the longest side of the image.
Returning the smallest image dimension is interpretable as the shortest side of the image.
The most frequent pixel value (histogram mode) relates to the dominant intensity, which is clinically interpretable.
The count of the most frequent pixel value is moderately interpretable as how dominant a particular intensity is.
Proportion of white pixels in a binary image directly maps to the fraction of foreground tissue or lesion area.
Proportion of black pixels in a binary image directly maps to the fraction of background area.
Number of unique pixel values relates to image complexity or number of distinct tissue types.
Mean image intensity is a fundamental and universally interpretable summary measure of brightness.
Median image intensity is a fundamental and universally interpretable summary of typical brightness.
Standard deviation of intensity is directly interpretable as overall image contrast or texture variability.
Maximum pixel intensity is directly interpretable as the brightest point in the image.
Minimum pixel intensity is directly interpretable as the darkest point in the image.
Conditional selection between two values based on a condition is moderately interpretable as a decision rule.
Mean intensity in a localized patch is directly interpretable as average brightness in a specific image region.
Standard deviation in a localized patch is directly interpretable as local texture variability.
Minimum value in a local patch is directly interpretable as the darkest spot in a region of interest.
Maximum value in a local patch is directly interpretable as the brightest spot in a region of interest.
Sum of values in a local patch is interpretable as total signal or intensity load in a region.
Median value in a local patch is directly interpretable as the typical intensity in a region of interest.
Range (max minus min) in a local patch is directly interpretable as local contrast in a region.
Local contrast between a center patch and surrounding ring is highly interpretable as lesion-versus-background contrast.
Local energy as mean squared intensity is somewhat interpretable but the squared nature adds abstraction.
Local entropy as a measure of intensity diversity is moderately interpretable as textural complexity.
Mean intensity in a small 5% patch at a specific location is directly interpretable as focal brightness.
Standard deviation in a small 5% patch is directly interpretable as fine-scale local texture variability.
Minimum in a small 5% patch is directly interpretable as the darkest point in a small focal area.
Maximum in a small 5% patch is directly interpretable as the brightest point in a small focal area.
Sum in a small 5% patch is interpretable as total signal in a focal area.
Median in a small 5% patch is directly interpretable as typical intensity in a small focal area.
Range in a small 5% patch is directly interpretable as local contrast in a small focal area.
Center-versus-ring contrast in a small 5% patch is interpretable as focal lesion contrast.
Energy in a small 5% patch is moderately interpretable but the squared nature adds abstraction.
Entropy in a small 5% patch measures textural complexity in a focal area.
Mean intensity in a 10% patch is directly interpretable as average brightness in a moderate focal area.
Standard deviation in a 10% patch is directly interpretable as local texture variability in a moderate area.
Minimum in a 10% patch is directly interpretable as the darkest point in a moderate focal area.
Maximum in a 10% patch is directly interpretable as the brightest point in a moderate focal area.
Sum in a 10% patch is interpretable as total signal in a moderate focal area.
Median in a 10% patch is directly interpretable as typical intensity in a moderate focal area.
Range in a 10% patch is directly interpretable as local contrast in a moderate focal area.
Center-versus-ring contrast in a 10% patch is interpretable as moderate-scale lesion contrast.
Energy in a 10% patch is moderately interpretable but the squared nature adds abstraction.
Entropy in a 10% patch measures textural complexity in a moderate focal area.
Mean intensity in a large 20% patch is directly interpretable as average brightness across a broad region.
Standard deviation in a 20% patch is directly interpretable as broad-scale texture variability.
Minimum in a 20% patch is directly interpretable as the darkest point across a broad area.
Maximum in a 20% patch is directly interpretable as the brightest point across a broad area.
Sum in a 20% patch is interpretable as total signal across a broad area.
Median in a 20% patch is directly interpretable as typical intensity across a broad area.
Range in a 20% patch is directly interpretable as broad-scale contrast.
Center-versus-ring contrast in a 20% patch is interpretable as large-scale lesion-versus-background contrast.
Energy in a 20% patch is moderately interpretable but the squared nature adds abstraction.
Entropy in a 20% patch measures broad-scale textural complexity.
Left-versus-right intensity contrast is interpretable as lateral asymmetry in a local region.
Top-versus-bottom intensity contrast is interpretable as vertical asymmetry in a local region.
Diagonal Haar contrast for main diagonal is less intuitively interpretable for a clinician.
Diagonal Haar contrast for anti-diagonal is less intuitively interpretable for a clinician.
Center-versus-surround contrast directly maps to lesion prominence against background tissue.
Horizontal three-band Haar contrast is a technical feature without immediate clinical intuition.
Vertical three-band Haar contrast is a technical feature without immediate clinical intuition.
Orientation coherence of gradient fields is moderately interpretable as structural regularity or fiber alignment.
Dominant gradient orientation bin is a technical concept that requires understanding of directional analysis.
Proportion of energy at 0-degree orientation is a technical directional measure not immediately clinical.
Proportion of energy at 45-degree orientation is a technical directional measure not immediately clinical.
Proportion of energy at 90-degree orientation is a technical directional measure not immediately clinical.
Proportion of energy at 135-degree orientation is a technical directional measure not immediately clinical.
How widely orientation energy is distributed could relate to tissue isotropy but requires interpretation effort.

Minimum GLCM IDM across angles is a highly technical metric.
Maximum GLCM IDM across angles is a highly technical metric.

Standard deviation of GLCM ASM across angles is a highly technical metric.
Minimum GLCM ASM across angles is a highly technical metric.
Maximum GLCM ASM across angles is a highly technical metric.

Standard deviation of GLCM entropy across angles is a technical texture metric.
Minimum GLCM entropy across angles is a technical texture metric.
Maximum GLCM entropy across angles is a technical texture metric.

GLCM max probability summed across angles is a technical aggregation.
Standard deviation of GLCM max probability across angles is a highly technical metric.
Minimum GLCM max probability across angles is a highly technical metric.
Maximum GLCM max probability across angles is a moderately technical metric.

Standard deviation of GLCM energy across angles is a highly technical metric.
Minimum GLCM energy across angles is a highly technical metric.
Maximum GLCM energy across angles is a moderately technical texture metric.
